r.문화권·종교: Korean · Protestant, Buddhist and Catholic, more than half with no religion
r.경제 체제: Export-driven market economy · chips, cars, batteries, shipbuilding
r.주식시장 시가총액: $2.8 trillion, 147% of GDP (2025, listed domestic companies)
r.Big Mac index: $3.84 for a Big Mac, 38% below the US price of $6.22 (Jul 2026, The Economist)
r.Consumer price level: 62% of the US level (2025, World Bank, household consumption at purchasing power parity against the market exchange rate)
r.정치 구도: A presidential system led by a directly elected president for a single five-year term, with a unicameral National Assembly that decides laws and the budget. A two-party standoff between the Democratic Party and the People Power Party has continued. The Constitutional Court rules on impeachments, the dissolution of parties and the constitutionality of laws, giving it great influence over politics. After the declaration of martial law in December 2024 the president was impeached, and an early presidential election was held in June 2025. Debate on a constitutional amendment to change the presidential term keeps coming up.

t.why: It makes a large share of the world's memory chips and has become a key supplier for the AI boom, and its exports of cars, batteries, ships and defense equipment have grown too. A US ally and a member of the G20, it joined the OECD in 1996. It is held up as a rare case of a country that went from receiving aid to giving it. Sitting on the southern half of the Korean Peninsula, surrounded by China, Japan, Russia and North Korea, balancing between the great powers is a major task of its diplomacy. As Korean dramas, music and films have won global popularity, its cultural influence has grown too.
t.rel: It has faced North Korea militarily for more than 70 years since the 1953 armistice. The United States is its ally; with Japan it clashes over history but cooperates on security and the economy; and China is its biggest trading partner.
t.know: Nearly half of all Koreans have one of three surnames: Kim, Lee or Park. Since 2019, more than half the population has lived in the capital region of Seoul, Gyeonggi and Incheon, which covers about 12% of the land.
etext: It is one of the few countries that make memory chips, ships, batteries, displays, cars, petrochemicals and steel all at a world-leading level. Large business groups make big investment decisions quickly, backed by a dense network of parts suppliers.

With almost no natural resources, it imports most of its oil, gas and minerals and processes them for sale. A high level of education and fast learning of technology are the basis of its competitiveness.
Exports of cultural products such as games, music, dramas, cosmetics and food are growing.

Exports are concentrated in chips and on China and the United States, so the economy swings widely. The world's lowest birth rate, rapid aging and the gap between big business and small firms are major challenges.
